name: Draft Japanese PR TIMES press releases from a form with OpenAI

parameters.content:
## Draft Japanese PR TIMES press releases from a form with OpenAI

### How it works

This workflow collects press release inputs through a form, enriches them with preset company information, and sends the combined context to an OpenAI-powered LLM chain. The AI drafts a Japanese PR TIMES-style press release and returns structured sections. It is told to use only the facts entered in the form, and anything it inferred is listed under "Points to check". The workflow then checks the subtitle length (PR TIMES limit: 100 characters), removes duplicate keywords, warns about announcement types that PR TIMES often rejects, and displays the final draft on the form completion page for review.

PR TIMES is a Japanese press release service, so the draft, the form examples, and the sample company details are in Japanese.

### Setup steps

- Update the company information in the **Set Company Information** node: company_name, company_hq, ceo, company_overview, and contact. These values are inserted into the release as-is.
- Connect valid OpenAI credentials to the **OpenAI GPT-5 Mini** node and confirm the selected model is available for your account.
- Click **Execute workflow**, open the form, and submit an announcement.

### Customization

You can adjust the form fields, the writing rules in **Draft Press Release**, the subtitle length threshold, the required keywords, and the final display fields to match different brands or release formats.

## Collect company context

Starts the workflow from a press release request form and adds fixed company profile details that will be used in the draft.

## Generate structured draft

Uses the LLM chain with the OpenAI chat model and structured output parser to create a Japanese PR TIMES-style press release draft in defined sections.

## Validate and show draft

Checks generated title and subtitle fields, calculates subtitle length and warnings, then presents the completed draft for review.

assignments.name: style_rules
assignments.value: Use the polite desu/masu style. Keep sentences short. Avoid exaggeration and overly strong claims. If the product name has a reading, add it in parentheses on first mention only.

messageValues.message:
You are a corporate PR writer. Using ONLY the material provided, write a press release draft for PR TIMES, a Japanese press release distribution service. Write every output field in Japanese.

Rules:
1. Never invent numbers, results, company names, people, or proper nouns that are not in the material. If something is missing, do not fill it in; list it in check_points instead.
2. Avoid claims that need evidence, such as 「業界初」「No.1」「必ず」「唯一」.
3. title: include the company name or product category, the product name in 「」, and what was done. Make the benefit to the reader clear.
4. subtitle: 60 to 100 Japanese characters. Do not repeat the title; add context such as the audience, what becomes possible, or the background.
5. lead: start with 「{company name}（{location}、{representative}）は、」, include the announcement date, and keep it to 2 or 3 sentences. On first mention you may write the product as {category}「{product name}」, using only category words found in the one-line product description. Add a reading in parentheses only on first mention.
6. body: each heading is one line starting with 「■ 」, in this order: ■ 背景 / ■ 特長 / (other content) / ■ お試し・お申し込み / ■ 今後の予定 / ■ 代表コメント / ■ 製品について.
   - You may add a short phrase to the background heading, e.g. 「■ 背景：…」.
   - Omit any heading whose material is (not provided). Put only future plans under 今後の予定; trial or application information goes under お試し・お申し込み.
   - For "Anything else to include", create headings that fit the content (e.g. ■ 質問の例, ■ ご利用の入口, ■ 料金). Keep every fact and do not change its meaning.
   - Write in polite です・ます prose. Use bullet lines starting with 「・」 only for 特長 and for material that is already a list. Do not use Markdown (#, **, tables).
   - If the key points for the CEO comment are (not provided), omit ■ 代表コメント entirely. Never write a comment the representative did not give.
   - The CEO comment may rephrase the key points naturally but must not add facts. End it with a new line 「（{company name} {representative's title and name}）」.
   - Under ■ 製品について, use the one-line product description word for word, followed by the related URL if given. If the description is (not provided), omit this heading and add a note in Japanese to check_points saying that the ■ 製品について section was omitted because no description was given. Never describe what the product does with words that are not in the material.
7. keywords: exactly 10, no duplicates. Put every must-include keyword first, unchanged; fill the rest with the product name, category, and problem words.
8. check_points (in Japanese): only about this draft. (a) expressions you inferred that are not in the material (quote the sentence in 「」), (b) headings omitted or thin because material was missing, (c) statements to fact-check before publishing (numbers, prices, dates, claimed capabilities). Do not list generic topics such as pricing or security if the draft does not mention them. At most 5. Re-read the draft for words that are not in the material before deciding. Use an empty array if there are none.
9. Do not write the company overview or the press contact. Fixed values are inserted later.

assignments.name: subtitle_warning
assignments.value: ={{ $json.output.subtitle.length > 100 ? '⚠️ サブタイトルが ' + $json.output.subtitle.length + ' 文字です（上限100文字）。/ The subtitle is ' + $json.output.subtitle.length + ' characters (PR TIMES limit: 100).' : '' }}

assignments.name: type_warning
assignments.value: ={{ $('When Form Submitted').item.json.announcement_type.startsWith('資料公開') ? '⚠️ PR TIMES では、ノウハウ資料やチェックリストを「公開した」こと自体が主題のリリースは掲載されないことがあります。新しい取り組みや成果が主題になっているか確かめてください。/ PR TIMES may not publish a release whose main news is only that a guide or checklist was published. Make sure the main topic is a new initiative or result.' : '' }}

assignments.name: keywords
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const seen = new Set(); return $json.output.keywords.map(k => String(k).trim()).filter(k => { const key = k.replace(/[（(].*?[）)]/g, '').replace(/\s/g, '').toLowerCase(); if (!key || seen.has(key)) return false; seen.add(key); return true; }).slice(0, 10).join('、'); })() }}

assignments.name: keyword_count
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const seen = new Set(); return $json.output.keywords.map(k => String(k).trim()).filter(k => { const key = k.replace(/[（(].*?[）)]/g, '').replace(/\s/g, '').toLowerCase(); if (!key || seen.has(key)) return false; seen.add(key); return true; }).slice(0, 10).length; })() }}
